topic: What actually happens in a Mentorsy diagnostic session

scenes.voiceover: By the time a Year 10 report shows a problem, the gap is usually two years old.
scenes.image_prompt: A school corridor with lockers, empty

scenes.voiceover: That is what a diagnostic session is for. Not a test. A map.
scenes.image_prompt: A hand drawn diagram on plain paper, pen beside it

scenes.voiceover: Our mentors work backwards through the Cambridge curriculum until the answers stop being wrong.
scenes.image_prompt: A student at a study desk by a window working through a page

scenes.voiceover: Usually it sits three or four topics earlier than anyone expected.
scenes.image_prompt: Open textbook pages fanned across a table

scenes.voiceover: Find that line and the next two years get easier. Miss it and the report repeats itself.
scenes.image_prompt: A closed exercise book on an empty school desk

caption:
A diagnostic is not a test. It is a map.

By the time a report flags a problem in IGCSE or A Level Mathematics, the gap is usually two years old. Our mentors work backwards through the Cambridge curriculum until the answers stop being wrong.

It is almost always earlier than parents expect.

Save this before the next report evening.
alt_text: An empty school corridor and study desk, on mapping gaps in the Cambridge maths curriculum
